discovery: Spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots: proposal and experimental realization of coherent single-electron spin control for quantum computing

nominees.name: David P. DiVincenzo
nominees.affiliation: Forschungszentrum Jülich and RWTH Aachen University, Germany

nominees.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
nominees.affiliation: QuTech, Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

subfield: Condensed matter physics / quantum information (semiconductor spin qubits)
motivation: In 1998 Loss and DiVincenzo proposed that the spin of a single electron confined in a semiconductor quantum dot could serve as a qubit, with exchange coupling between neighbouring dots providing two-qubit gates. This insight turned the electron spin, the most elementary quantum two-level system in solid-state physics, into a practical architecture. Vandersypen and co-workers then realised it experimentally: single-shot spin readout, coherent single-spin rotations, and high-fidelity one- and two-qubit gates in GaAs and later isotopically purified silicon, including programmable multi-qubit processors. Together these works established that individual spins in a solid can be isolated, controlled and entangled at the fundamental quantum limit, and that this can be done with the materials and fabrication methods of the semiconductor industry. The field they created now underpins a worldwide effort toward scalable, CMOS-compatible quantum computers.
